summary: qwen-mt-turbo (the production translator) retires 2026-10-10. A successor must pass strict masked-name token survival, match turbo-class quality, fit the 5-minute cron budget, AND price sensibly — every entry below now carries its list price so quality and cost can be weighed together. The masked set uses ASCII [[n]] markers since the 2026-09-29 identity spike (the PUA scheme broke GLM-family and nemotron tokenizers). DeepSeek (both models) and glm-5.3-flash re-passed 10/10 on brackets and are reinstated; the OpenRouter models' bracket re-measurement is still blocked on OpenRouter credits, and identical open-weight models are now verified equivalent across providers (within ~3 chrF) and collapsed into one row on the site. Disqualified below does NOT mean bad at translation — the DeepSeek models are the best pure translators measured — it means unusable for THIS production pipeline, which masks people's names before translation and restores them afterwards.

why: 10/10 masked-name token survival in both directions
73.71 chrF id->en (+1.8 over the retiring qwen-mt-turbo, +2.0 over the QwenCloud interim pick)
84.66 chrF en->id (turbo-class; direction re-measured on the balanced 78-segment set)
non-thinking: no reasoning leakage, no mid-sweep stalls, 1.4-1.6 s/segment

cheapest token-safe model measured: $0.0875 in / $0.35 out per M tokens (models.dev) — a full two-direction 78-segment sweep costs about two cents; only gemma-4-31b-it lists comparably ($0.09/$0.34) among the 10/10-survival models

alternatives.why: best token-safe id->en off QwenCloud (74.21, Kagi-level), but the price buys it: $0.60/$1.92 per M tokens — 5-8x the primary per sweep. Take it only if id->en quality is worth the premium or as a second vendor for drift checks
73.39 id->en, 10/10 survival both directions, maker-diverse from the primary — priced mid-pack at $0.45/$2.25 per M (roughly 5x the primary per sweep)
72.72 id->en, 10/10 survival both directions, permissive Gemma licence, and the only price-peer of the primary ($0.09/$0.34 per M) — the budget-switchover pick if OpenRouter pricing shifts

alternatives.role: reinstated quality pick — pending the full re-sweep
alternatives.why: the best raw translation quality measured (77.10 chrF id->en, 87.05 en->id) now also survives 10/10 in both directions on the [[n]] bracket scheme; its original disqualification was the PUA token scheme plus 1024-token truncation, both fixed on 2026-09-29 (docs/identity-spike.md). Cost cuts both ways: $0.15/$0.60 per M at the official API (2x the primary), but the same open weights list at $0.0763/$0.1526 on OpenRouter and verify within ~3 chrF of first-party — the cheapest listing of any token-safe model once measured. The same weights on Cloudflare cost 3x first-party ($0.44/$1.32): provider choice matters more than model choice here. Formal ranking waits until the OpenRouter models are re-measured on brackets

alternatives.role: reinstated after the scheme fix — pending re-rank
alternatives.why: 10/10 bracket survival in both directions (was 7/10 on PUA tokens). List price $0.15/$0.50 per M looks mid-pack, but both known hosts mandate reasoning, so every call bills ~1000+ hidden thinking tokens as output — effective cost roughly 2-3x list, with Cloudflare's serving also ~3x slower than OpenRouter's (11.5 vs 4.0 s/sentence). deepseek-v4-pro also passes 10/10 both directions

alternatives.role: zero-cost failover tier (with xiaomi/mimo-v2.6-flash, cohere/command-a-plus, upstage/solar-mini4)
alternatives.why: all four Cline free-promotion models pass 10/10 bracket survival in both directions at $0 — no credits held on any gateway. glm-5.3-prime leads them (74.27 chrF id->en / 72.72 en->id, 2.7-4.4 s/s with reasoning on), mimo-v2.6-flash is close (73.36/72.57); command-a-plus is the fastest hosted model measured (0.9 s/s) but weak id->en (67.14); solar-mini4 trails (71.60/67.33). Mid-field quality — an emergency tier if paid gateways are all unavailable, not a successor. The promos rotate: verify an id still meters zero before relying on it

disqualified.reason: on the [[n]] bracket scheme it survives 10/10 en->id but dropped an intermittent marker id->en (9/10) — much improved from the PUA era (which broke it outright), but a 1-in-20 drop rate keeps it out of the outage-failover seat
fail id->en masked survival (2/10, 1/10); qwen-mt-lite passes raw but inherits the family's non-raisable caps and single-vendor retirement risk

same open weights as or-qwen3-30b-a3b-2507 but Cloudflare's fp8 build measures 5.8 chrF below OpenRouter's full-precision serving en->id (67.84 vs 73.65) — quantization damage beyond the ~3 chrF cross-provider parity band, so it is not collapsed with its full-precision twin and is not a candidate

caveats: 2026-09-30 cross-provider parity: identical open-weight models measured at several providers land within ~3 chrF per direction (temperature 0 leaves serving-stack variance; ~0.5 chrF run-to-run nondeterminism on Cloudflare). The site collapses such runs into one row — primary provider's scores, provider badges, cheapest listing in the cost cell (site/tools/models.ts holds the rules)

2026-09-29 scheme migration: the masked set now uses ASCII [[n]] markers (the identity spike showed PUA tokens break GLM-family and nemotron tokenizers); PUA-era survival rows are archived and not comparable. The OpenRouter models keep their old PUA-era survival numbers until the account is funded again — their brackets survival is not yet measured (gemma-4-31b-it excepted: 10/10 all schemes in the spike)

all prices are list (models.dev + provider catalogues, 2026-09-29/30) per M tokens in/out; the site's Cost column shows the cheapest provider per collapsed model — check it before any spending decision, prices drift

token-safe models run 1.4-2.7 s/segment sequential: a 300-segment entry needs 3-4 concurrent requests to hold the 5-minute cron budget; QwenCloud's qwen-flash (0.46 s/s, 10/10 survival, raisable limits) remains the sub-minute option if staying on QwenCloud
the survival assertion + review flags stay regardless of model: the turbo baseline production trusted also failed the adversarial probe set
qwen-mt-turbo retires 2026-10-10; until the switch, it remains the production model
